thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High tail latency observed for /v1/generate (us-west1) — p99 > 2.5s, queuing increasing

alex: saw the page. I'm looking at runtime dashboard now. p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 600ms, p99 spiking to 2.6s. queue length on gpu-pool-3 jumped from ~10 -> ~120 over last 6m.

maria: thanks. any obvious deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy: model-serving:rollout/continuous-batching-v2 succeeded at 2024-06-08T14:03:20Z (build #2184)

alex: hmm deploy happened ~14:03. correlates with spike start. continuous-batching-v2 increases batching window under high concurrency to squeeze throughput — might be overshooting for latency-sensitive routes.

jamie: link to heatmap: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serving/batching?panel=tail-latency (shortlink) — looks like long-seq customers hit heavy queueing.

kevin: proposed mitigations (live):
- reduce batch_max_tokens from 1024 -> 256 for route /v1/generate in us-west1
- lower batch_timeout_ms from 30ms -> 10ms (trades throughput for lower latency)
- flip feature-flag to disable continuous batching for requests with prompt_tokens < 512
- apply soft rate-limit at edge for top-10 noisy customers: 120rps -> 60rps

alex: agree. priorities: (1) cut batch size & timeout to drain queues, (2) edge rate-limit to stop runaway clients, (3) targeted flag to prevent regression.

kevin: executing 1 & 2 now.

kevin: running CLI to patch runtime config:
```bash
rwinfctl runtime update --region us-west1 --pool gpu-pool-3 \
  --set batch_max_tokens=256 --set batch_timeout_ms=10
```

kevin: also applying feature flag change (temp):
```bash
rwinfctl flags set continuous_batching_enabled=false --region us-west1 --filter "route:/v1/generate and prompt_tokens<512"
```

deploy-bot: runbook-step: feature-flag toggle succeeded (ops-agent-47)

maria: I'm watching metrics. queue length dropping from 120 -> 18 in last 2m. p99 down to 1.1s and still trending down. p95 now ~320ms.

alex: good. note: we will see some increase in token-cost because smaller batches, but customer latency matters more here.

cs-ops: heads up — customer telemetry shows 3 customers (acme-inc, beta-studio, fast-ai) saw elevated 429/limited errors when we applied rate-limit to noisy clients. They've been flagged.

maria: how many 429 events?

cs-ops: acme-inc ~ 220 429s in last 5m, beta-studio ~ 78, fast-ai ~ 44. Most on long-seq jobs.

alex: ok we'll temporarily bump their quota to reduce customer impact while keeping global shape. Kevin, can you add delta quotas for premium customers?

kevin: applying per-customer override for acme-inc and beta-studio for next 30m:
```bash
rwinfctl quota update --customer acme-inc --region us-west1 --requests_per_min=600
rwinfctl quota update --customer beta-studio --region us-west1 --requests_per_min=300
```

kevin: overrides applied. monitoring.

maria: seeing 429s for acme-inc drop to <10 in last minute. thanks.

jamie: note for post-incident: continuous-batching-v2 has heuristics that treat long-context workloads as high-value for throughput. We should revisit the threshold — maybe do route-aware defaults.

alex: agreed. for now we revert risky global defaults and schedule follow-up: rollback/analysis.

alex: handoff to next oncall @kevin — summary:
- incident: tail latency spike caused by continuous-batching-v2 rollout interacting with long-seq customer traffic
- live mitigations performed: reduced batch_max_tokens ->256, batch_timeout_ms ->10, disabled continuous batching for small prompts, applied edge rate-limits, temporary per-customer quota overrides for impacted customers
- current state: p99 ~ 0.9s, queue length ~6, throughput ~stable. Some 429s observed briefly but per-customer overrides reduced customer impact.
- residual risk: increased per-token cost and slight throughput loss while mitigations in place. if traffic continues to spike we might need to scale pool or enable burst-capacity.
- follow-ups: rollback continuous-batching-v2 or patch heuristics; add route-aware batching thresholds; postmortem and action items.

kevin: taking it. I will keep the mitigations for 30m and then gradually re-evaluate. tagging eng-runtime +eng-platform for follow-up.

maria: I'll alert CS to message the impacted customers and offer an explanation + ETA. @cs-ops can you copy/paste a short note?

cs-ops: sure — posting to customer thread now: "We saw a transient latency issue affecting some long-running requests in us-west1. We've applied mitigations (batching config & temporary quota adjustments) and are monitoring. Expect normal service within ~30 minutes. If customers still see issues, escalate to support@redwood.com." :thumbsup:

alex: thanks. I'll file incident ticket and assign for postmortem: INC-2024-2467. Please include the graphs, deploy timeline, and the exact flag toggles/CLI commands we ran.

kevin: noted. I'll leave a runbook snippet in the ticket with the exact commands used.

jamie: small note — we should add a canary for batching rollouts that simulates long-seq load to catch this pre-prod. adding to backlog.

kevin: okay leaving shift in 10m — if anything regresses ping me.

alex: thanks team. I'll follow up if we need full escalation. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: handoff: alex -> kevin recorded at 2024-06-08T15:10:30Z

kevin: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see new spikes. scheduling postmortem meeting in #incidents for tomorrow 11:00PT.
